items.name: HL · Order items → stock movements + confirmation
items.what: 2.4 Part A: a website order arrives as JSON on a custom webhook, the Iterator splits its items array into one bundle per item, each item adds a negative row to Stock_Movements (so a SUMIFS formula keeps stock right, even when a product appears twice), and a Text aggregator with the Iterator as source module squeezes the items back into one confirmation email per order.
build: 1 · Webhooks › Custom webhook: add a new webhook named HL website orders; Maximum number of results = 1. Redetermine the data structure by sending the sample order below.
3 · Google Sheets › Add a Row: Sheet = Stock_Movements; A date = {{formatDate(now; "YYYY-MM-DD")}}; B order_id = {{1.order_id}}; C sku = {{2.sku}}; D qty_change = {{-1 * 2.qty}}.
4 · Tools › Text aggregator: Source module = 2. Iterator (not the webhook); Row separator = New row; Text = {{2.qty}}× {{2.name}} · ₦{{formatNumber(2.qty * 2.unit_price; 0; "."; ",")}}.

5 · Gmail › Send an Email: To = {{ifempty(1.customer.email; "orders@harvestlane.example")}}; Subject = Harvest Lane · order {{1.order_id}} confirmed; Content (HTML) = Hi {{1.customer.name}}, thank you! Your order {{1.order_id}}:
{{replace(4.text; newline; "

Delivery fee: ₦{{formatNumber(1.delivery_fee; 0; "."; ",")}}
Total: ₦{{formatNumber(1.total; 0; "."; ",")}}

Scenario settings: instant (webhook) trigger, scheduling ON = Immediately. Scenario name: HL · Order items → stock movements + confirmation.
setup: Add a Stock_Movements tab: A date, B order_id, C sku, D qty_change (negative for sales, positive for supplier deliveries).
In Products, make stock_qty a formula: =opening_stock + SUMIFS(Stock_Movements!D:D, Stock_Movements!C:C, A2) (adjust opening_stock to its cell, e.g. D2), and fill it down.
In Make: Scenarios → Create a new scenario → the three-dot menu at the bottom → Import Blueprint → choose this file.

Click module 1 → Add → name the webhook HL website orders → Save, copy its URL, then click Redetermine data structure and send the sample order (below) with a tool like Postman or the 1.4 test page. The webhook URL is a secret: keep it out of public page code.
Connect Google Sheets (module 3) and Gmail (module 5) with the business Google account and pick the Stock_Movements tab.
Check module 4's Source module is the Iterator. Switch scheduling ON (Immediately).

Stock_Movements gets three rows (TOM-CRATE −2, TOM-CRATE −1, ONI-BAG −3), Products shows tomatoes down by exactly 3, and one email lists 2× Tomatoes · ₦25,000, 1× Tomatoes · ₦12,500, 3× Onions · ₦12,000.

walk.title: Build it: stock that updates itself
walk.sample: Website order HL-0071 · Mrs Adebayo · 2× Tomatoes, 1× Tomatoes, 3× Onions · total 51,000

steps.say: First, the sheet. Stock_Movements gets one row per change, and stock in Products is a SUMIFS formula over it, so no update can ever overwrite another.
Website orders arrive as JSON on a custom webhook. Send the sample order once so Make learns its shape. Treat that webhook address as a secret.
show: Webhooks › Custom webhook: HL website orders

steps.say: One order, three products inside it. The Iterator pulls the accordion open: one bundle per item, so each can be handled on its own.
Each item adds a row to Stock_Movements, with a negative quantity for a sale. We add rows instead of overwriting stock.
show: Google Sheets › Add a Row · Sheet: Stock_Movements

steps.say: This is why: when tomatoes appear twice in one order, an overwrite design reads stale stock and loses a crate. Two movement rows simply add up.
Everything between the iterator and the aggregator runs, and costs a credit, once per item. Three items means three Add a Row credits.
Now squeeze the accordion shut with a Text aggregator: one line per item, joined by new lines.
show: Tools › Text aggregator · Row separator: New row

steps.say: Set the source module to the Iterator, not the webhook. The wrong source is the classic bug that mixes one customer's items into another's email.
One Gmail module after the aggregator sends one confirmation per order, listing every item, the delivery fee and the total.
Inside the email, we turn the aggregator's new lines into line breaks so the list reads properly.
It's an instant trigger, so scheduling is set to Immediately. The six p.m. summary is a separate scenario using the same squeeze, with Search Rows as the source.
show: Name: HL · Order items → stock movements + confirmation

walk.end: Post the sample order with tomatoes twice, then check for three movement rows, tomatoes down by exactly three, and one email.

items.name: HL · 6 p.m. daily summary
items.what: 2.4 Part B: every day at 18:00, Search Rows finds today's orders, a Numeric aggregator sums the totals, a second one counts the orders, a Text aggregator builds one line per order (all three with the search as source module), and Tolu gets one email, "Today: 17 orders · ₦412,500" plus the list, instead of forty alerts.
build: 1 · Google Sheets › Search Rows: business Google connection; Sheet = Orders; Table contains headers = Yes; Filter = created_at (column B) Contains {{formatDate(now; "YYYY-MM-DD")}}; Limit = 500.
2 · Tools › Numeric aggregator: Source module = 1. Search Rows; Aggregate function = SUM; Value = {{1.total}} (the plain number column, never a ₦-formatted one).
3 · Tools › Numeric aggregator: Source module = 1. Search Rows; Aggregate function = COUNT; Value = {{1.order_id}}.
4 · Tools › Text aggregator: Source module = 1. Search Rows; Row separator = New row; Text = {{1.order_id}} · {{1.customer_name}} · ₦{{formatNumber(1.total; 0; "."; ",")}}.

5 · Gmail › Send an Email: To = tolu@harvestlane.example; Subject = Today: {{3.result}} orders · ₦{{formatNumber(2.result; 0; "."; ",")}}; Content (HTML) = the same line, then

{{replace(4.text; newline; "
")}}.

If Make will not let modules 3 and 4 use module 1 as their source after another aggregator, use the lesson's alternative: 2 · Flow control › Array aggregator (source 1, fields order_id, customer_name, total), then count with {{length(2.array)}}, total with {{sum(map(2.array; "total"))}}, and the list with an Iterator on 2.array plus a Text aggregator sourced from that Iterator.
Scenario settings › Schedule: Every day at 18:00. Scheduling ON. Scenario name: HL · 6 p.m. daily summary.
setup: In Make, set your organisation and profile time zone to Africa/Lagos before running anything with dates (2.2).

Orders tab layout the blueprints assume (row 1 = headers): A order_id, B created_at, C customer_id, D customer_name, E delivery_date, F delivery_fee, G status, H items_total, I total (the 0.4 columns), then J phone, K channel, L delivery_window, M customer_email, N payment_link. If your columns differ, open each Google Sheets module after import and re-pick the columns; the build list names every field.
created_at must start with the date written as YYYY-MM-DD (for example 2026-10-12 09:41) so the Contains filter finds today's rows.
In Make: Scenarios → Create a new scenario → the three-dot menu at the bottom → Import Blueprint → choose this file.
Connect Google Sheets (module 1) and Gmail (module 5) with the business Google account; pick the spreadsheet and Orders tab, and confirm the filter column is created_at.
Open modules 2, 3 and 4 and check each Source module is 1. Search Rows.
Schedule: every day at 18:00, then switch scheduling ON. This is one of your two Free-plan active scenarios.
items.test: Add five rows to Orders with today's created_at (totals 26500, 13500, 82000, 9000, 40000) and one row dated yesterday. Run once: Search Rows shows 5, each aggregator 1, Gmail 1. One email arrives: "Today: 5 orders · ₦171,000" followed by five lines like HL-0061 · Mrs Adebayo · ₦26,500. Yesterday's row is not listed. Check a hand-added total and count against the sheet.
